alt: Two curves of in-place concrete strength over 72 hours. The June pour crosses the 15 MPa strip line at 21 hours, the January pour at 39 hours.
post:
When can the formwork come off? Many sites use a fixed number of days: too cautious in June, risky in a cold January.

I built an open-source version of the idea behind embedded concrete sensors: temperature loggers at three depths in the slab, the maturity method (Nurse-Saul and Arrhenius equivalent age), a strength curve calibrated from lab cylinders, and alerts for frost risk and core-to-surface temperature difference. A LoRaWAN/BLE payload and JS decoder are included.

I ran it on simulated 30 cm slabs driven by real hourly air temperature for Zurich (Open-Meteo archive, January and June 2024). The same mix reaches the 15 MPa strip threshold after 21 h in June and 39 h in a protected January pour, 18 h later. The choice of datum temperature or activation energy moves the January answer by 5 to 10 h and the June answer by about 1 to 2 h. Repeating the lab calibration with 60 noise draws changes the strip time by only 0.4 h (sd).

What is not verified: no real concrete, sensor or lab test was used, the thresholds are example values, and maturity estimates are not valid once concrete freezes.

Which decision would you want a sensor to make for you first, stripping, post-tensioning or frost protection?

Code: https://github.com/VB-Builds/concrete-maturity-lab
